messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1767204321 — Elevated 5xx/latency observed for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in us-east-1 (APIGW/ELB upstream). Affecting customer requests and embeddings ingestion. Pager routed to oncall.
raj: seeing 502/503 spike across multiple edge ELBs, error rate ~12% for last 3m. Dashboards: https://redwood.app/d/ingest/us-east1
matt_sre: acked. I'm pulling logs from the api-gateway and ingress ELBs now. Can someone confirm Dedicated pool health in us-east-1?
aj: Dedicated pools show increased queue latency, a few nodes reporting OOM/restarts ~ 10m ago. No rollout changes in last hour.
emma_eng: no deploys from engine teams in last 2 hours. I +1 that it's upstream.
olivia_prod: PS: we have 2 paying customers on Dedicated in us-east-1 with latency-sensitive SLAs. Notified CSMs and opened incident communication thread.
matt_sre: running tcpdump/conntrack on a problematic node: seeing TCP reset spikes to APIGW IP ranges. Suspecting AWS regional control-plane or edge issue.
raj: opened AWS support ticket (case #123456789). AWS status page shows "degraded" for APIGW in us-east-1.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: https://pd.example/INCIDENT-23456 assigned to matt_sre. Escalation in 15m if not resolved.
emma_eng: mitigation idea: route new requests away from us-east-1 via smart routing policy (region failover) to us-west-2 for hosted API and to fallback Dedicated pools. Who can flip the route?
aj: I can change routing policy in the router service. Will start a gradual regional failover and increase retry budget to 3 with exponential backoff. Command: `redwoodctl routing set-priority us-west-2,us-east-1 --strategy=gradual --duration=10m`
matt_sre: also enabling prefix caching on edge (force-hit cached responses for GETs) to reduce downstream load. Patch: `edge-config set caching:prefix=true`.
olivia_prod: please add a note to status page: intermittent 5xx in us-east-1, partial failover in progress. I posted draft update to customers.
emma_eng: important: embeddings ingestion pipeline is write-heavy and can't be safely rerouted. Consider pausing ingestion for non-critical customers to protect downstream.
raj: pausing non-priority ingestion jobs now. `jobs pause --tag=ingest-background --region=us-east-1`.
matt_sre: routing change started — shifting ~60% of traffic to us-west-2 progressively. Monitoring error rate.
raj: error rate dropping from 12% -> 6% after 4m. Latency still elevated for in-flight sessions pinned to us-east-1.
emma_eng: can we hot-swap tokens for external auth provider? Some failures are 403 from third-party auth service when refreshing tokens via APIGW.
matt_sre: switching token refresh path to use regional cache. `auth-proxy set token_cache=true --fallback=static`.
aws-support: AWS update: investigating APIGW ELB connection resets in us-east-1, mitigation in progress. Will update every 15 minutes.
olivia_prod: customer-impact note: a handful of customers on Dedicated may see degraded throughput; we're offering temporary credits if SLA impacted. CS team standing by.
raj: starting handoff prep: compiling timeline + runbook. Current actions: routing failover in progress, ingestion paused for background jobs, prefix caching enabled, auth-proxy fallback enabled, AWS ticket open.
emma_eng: quick postmortem items to capture: why some Dedicated nodes restarted (OOM) — investigate autoscaler and memory pressure under partial failover.
oncall-next: I'm coming on in 10m to take over. Need the exact list of customers affected and mitigation steps to continue.
matt_sre: adding list to the incident doc and transferring pager. `incidenttools handoff --to=oncall-next --notes="routing->us-west-2, ingestion paused, caching enabled, AWS case 123456789"`
oncall-next: got it. I will continue monitoring for 2 hours and coordinate with AWS. If error rate >5% for 10m, escalate to infra lead.
olivia_prod: status page updated and customer comms sent. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — routing shift completed to 85% us-west-2, error rate stabilized at ~2.1% for last 5m. Leaving incident open for monitoring and postmortem.
raj: thanks team. Postmortem owner: emma_eng. Assigning follow-ups: autoscaler tuning, stronger prefix caching defaults, routing playbook update. Closing handoff to oncall-next.
oncall-next: acknowledged, monitoring window started.
